description: For **eight years**, France fought an independence insurrection on a territory it considered its own. The Algerian War brought down the Fourth Republic and left lasting scars.

hero.hook: Eight years of war that France has long refused to call a war.

blocks.text: The Algerian War (**1954-1962**) is one of the most painful chapters in 20th century French history. It is not just decolonization. For Paris, Algeria is not a distant colony: it is a part of France.

For eight years, the state faced the **FLN**, the National Liberation Front, which wanted independence. The crisis brought down the Fourth Republic and gave birth to the Fifth. Long called “events” or “maintenance of order”, this war leaves torn memories on both sides of the Mediterranean.

Conquered from **1830**, Algeria is divided from **1848** into . Leaving Algeria, for many, means amputating the national territory. In **1954**, there were approximately **9 million** Muslims and **1 million** Europeans, the . [[French departments]] [[The Blackfoot]]
Until **1999**, the French state legally refused the word “war”. We speak of “maintenance of order” operations, so as not to recognize FLN combatants as prisoners of war.

blocks.caption: FLN fighters during the Algerian War.

blocks.text: **May 8, 1945**, while Europe celebrates victory, the repression of demonstrations in Sétif and Guelma, in eastern Algeria, leaves thousands dead. **November 1, 1954**, “Red All Saints’ Day”: the FLN launches around sixty attacks. **François Mitterrand**, then Minister of the Interior, summed up the official line: “Algeria is France. »

In 1956, Parliament voted the [[special powers]]: the army received police powers. Nearly **400, 000** soldiers, many of them conscripts, crisscross the country facing the [[guerrilla warfare]] of the FLN, a war of ambushes and attacks.

blocks.caption: Algiers, 1957: urban warfare in the heart of the capital.

blocks.text: In **1957**, during the **battle of Algiers**, the paratroopers of General **Jacques Massu** dismantled the networks of bombers. Military victory, moral defeat: torture becomes a common tool to obtain information. In mainland France, the scandal grew. France is torn apart over the legitimacy of its own war.

**May 13, 1958**, Algiers rebels to keep “French Algeria”. **Charles de Gaulle** returns to power and founds the Fifth Republic. First seen as a savior of French sovereignty, he quickly understood that maintaining it was untenable. It is steering the country towards self-determination: letting Algerians choose their future.

blocks.caption: De Gaulle facing the Algerian question.

blocks.text: In April **1961**, the [[OAS]] tried to overthrow him. After the failure, the [[The generals' putsch (April 1961)]], Secret Army Organization, multiplies attacks to block any negotiations.

blocks.text: The Algerian War (**1954-1962**) ends the French colonial empire. It leaves a painful legacy: torture, exodus of the pieds-noirs, abandonment of the harkis.
